samples.xml_description:
<module id="RAM">
    <description>Implement a dual-port RAM with a depth of DEPTH and a bit width of WIDTH bits, with all data initialized to 000000. It has two groups of ports, respectively for reading data and writing data, and read and write operations can be carried out at the same time. When the read_en signal is 1, the read_data of the corresponding position is read through the read_addr signal and output; When the write_en signal is 1, data is written to the corresponding position through the write_addr signal and write-data signal.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="write_en">Write enable signal to initiate a write operation.</input>
        <input id="write_addr">Address for the write operation. Bit size is $clog2(DEPTH).</input>
        <input id="write_data">Data to be written to the RAM.</input>
        <input id="read_en">Read enable signal to initiate a read operation.</input>
        <input id="read_addr">Address for the read operation. Bit size is $clog2(DEPTH).</input>
        <output id="read_data">Output signal representing the data read from the RAM.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="WIDTH" value="6"/>
        <parameter id="DEPTH" value="8"/>
    </parameter_description>
    <implementation>internal_RAM Array:
The module includes a register array, internal_RAM. The array is defined as reg [WIDTH - 1 : 0] internal_RAM [DEPTH-1:0], allowing for DEPTH memory locations, each with a width of WIDTH bits.
Write Operation:
The first always block triggers on the positive edge of the clock signal (posedge clk) or the negative edge of the reset signal (negedge rst_n).
On reset, indicated by !rst_n, all memory locations in the internal_RAM array are cleared to 0.
If the write enable signal (write_en) is active, the data (write_data) is written to the internal_RAM array at the specified address (write_addr).
Read Operation:
The second always block triggers on the positive edge of the clock signal (posedge clk) or the negative edge of the reset signal (negedge rst_n).
On reset, indicated by !rst_n, the read_data register is cleared to 0.
If the read enable signal (read_en) is active, the data at the specified address (read_addr) in the internal_RAM array is assigned to the read_data register.
If the read enable signal is not active, the read_data register is cleared to 0.
</implementation>
</module>
